root_cause.text: The TCP-AO inbound MAC verification in `tcp_ao_verify_hash()` used `memcmp()` on authentication tags, causing data-dependent early-exit timing behavior instead of constant-time comparison.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (memcmp(phash, hash_buf, maclen))` to `if (crypto_memneq(phash, hash_buf, maclen))`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state this is needed “to prevent timing attacks” during MAC comparison.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make TCP_AO automatically select CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS so its required crypto utility support is always enabled.
intent_record.what: The Kconfig entry for TCP_AO was modified to add `select CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS` alongside the existing selected dependencies `CRYPTO` and `TCP_SIGPOOL`.
intent_record.how: Enabling TCP_AO will now automatically enable the CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS configuration option as well, ensuring the feature builds and runs with that required crypto utility library available instead of relying on it to be enabled separately or missing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Include crypto/utils.h so the file has access to required crypto utility definitions and avoids related build or symbol resolution problems.
intent_record.what: A new header include, <crypto/utils.h>, was added to the source file alongside the existing <crypto/hash.h> include.
intent_record.how: This makes declarations or helpers from the crypto utilities interface available during compilation, enabling the file to use symbols from that header and preventing build issues if such crypto utility definitions are required.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a constant-time hash comparison in TCP-AO verification to prevent timing leaks while preserving mismatch handling.
intent_record.what: The condition in tcp_ao_verify_hash() was changed from using memcmp(phash, hash_buf, maclen) to using crypto_memneq(phash, hash_buf, maclen) when comparing the received hash against the computed hash.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the hash verification still detects mismatches and enters the same failure path, but the comparison is now performed with a crypto-safe non-equality helper that avoids ordinary memcmp semantics, reducing timing side-channel leakage during MAC verification.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is specifically about replacing non-constant-time memcmp() with a constant-time crypto utility comparison. Enabling CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS and including crypto/utils.h directly supports access to that crypto utility functionality, so these changes are part of addressing the root cause.
The group directly replaces the non-constant-time MAC/tag comparison in TCP-AO verification with a constant-time comparison to eliminate the timing side channel described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This line performs TCP-AO MAC verification using memcmp(), which is not constant-time and can return early on the first differing byte, creating the timing side channel described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs inbound TCP-AO MAC verification with memcmp(), which is data-dependent and may exit on the first differing byte. That creates the timing side channel described in the root cause; a constant-time comparison is required for authentication tag verification.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full body of the relevant function `tcp_ao_verify_hash()` and shows exactly how inbound TCP-AO MACs are compared. The vulnerable construct is present in `tcp_ao_verify_hash()`: `if (memcmp(phash, hash_buf, maclen)) { ... return SKB_DROP_REASON_TCP_AOFAILURE; }`. Using `memcmp()` for authentication tag verification is the root cause described, because `memcmp()` is not constant-time and may exit early depending on the first differing byte, creating timing side-channel behavior. There is no constant-time comparison helper such as `crypto_memneq()` or similar in this function, so the fix is not present. Therefore this commit version contains the bug and is not yet fixed.
